<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919986_theRebbe_397" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919986_theRebbe_397__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the lion (Ari) ascended and destroyed Ariel so that the lion would come again and rebuild it, linking this to the revelation of the Keter above the chain of descent, which is aroused through the bitterness of exile.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is: "A lion ascended in the constellation of Leo and destroyed Ariel… so that a lion would come in the constellation of Leo and build Ariel,"</t>
    <t s="1">"For a lion will come"</t>
    <t s="2">[this is the Holy One, blessed be He, about whom it is written, "A lion has roared, who will not fear"]</t>
    <t s="3">this is the matter of the revelation of the Keter that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="4">And since the revelation that is above the chain of descent is through service that is above measure and limitation,</t>
    <t s="5">therefore, in order that "a lion will come" etc., it was necessary that "a lion ascended" etc.,</t>
    <t s="6">For the bitterness and pain that come from the straits of the exile are what arouse the service that is above limitation,</t>
    <t s="7">as mentioned above.</t>
    <t s="8">And therefore, specifically through the precedence of exile, "a lion will come" etc. and "build Ariel,"</t>
    <t s="9">the third Holy Temple.</t>
    <t s="10">And this is also the superiority of the future Holy Temple over the First Temple and the Second Temple,</t>
    <t s="11">that specifically in the third Holy Temple</t>
    <t s="12">(since it comes after the precedence of the final exile)</t>
    <t s="13">there will be in it</t>
    <t s="14">(the main)</t>
    <t s="15">the revelation of the aspect of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent</t>
    <t s="16">("a lion will come").</t>
    <t s="17">And this is the reason why the future Holy Temple will be in the aspect of eternity</t>
    <t s="18">(unlike the First Temple and the Second Temple, which were in the aspect of cessation),</t>
    <t s="19">because from the perspective of the revelation of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="20">the concept of cessation does not apply.</t>
    <t s="21">And this is what is stated,</t>
    <t s="22">"The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established, the Lord will reign forever and ever,"</t>
    <t s="23">and the explanation of this is</t>
    <t s="24">(as stated in the Emek HaMelech in the aforementioned discourse),</t>
    <t s="25">that because "the Sanctuary… Your hands have established,"</t>
    <t s="26">meaning that the future Holy Temple will be by the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself</t>
    <t s="27">[i.e., the aspect of Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent],</t>
    <t s="28">therefore, "the Lord will reign forever and ever,"</t>
    <t s="29">that it will be in the aspect of eternity.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the power for the service of "with all your might" during exile comes from the revelations of the First and Second Temples, which contained a foretaste of the future Temple.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, the power that exists during the time of exile for the service of "with all your might," through which the future Holy Temple will be,</t>
    <t s="1">comes from the revelations of the First Temple and the Second Temple that were before the exile.</t>
    <t s="2">For these revelations give the power to illuminate the darkness of exile with "a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light,"</t>
    <t s="3">to the point that through this, "night will shine like day"</t>
    <t s="4">in the future redemption.</t>
    <t s="5">And the reason for this</t>
    <t s="6">(that the First Temple and the Second Temple give the power for the service of "with all your might," through which the third Holy Temple will be)</t>
    <t s="7">is,</t>
    <t s="8">because even in the First Temple and the Second Temple</t>
    <t s="9">(even though there was cessation in them)</t>
    <t s="10">there was a foretaste of the third Holy Temple.</t>
    <t s="11">And likewise, this is also the case regarding the Mishkan, which was a foretaste of the future Holy Temple.</t>
    <t s="12">For although the Mishkan is called "Ohel" (tent),</t>
    <t s="13">a temporary dwelling</t>
    <t s="14">(unlike the Temple, which is called "Bayit" (house),</t>
    <t s="15">a permanent dwelling),</t>
    <t s="16">nevertheless, specifically the Mishkan,</t>
    <t s="17">since it was the handiwork of Moshe,</t>
    <t s="18">endures forever.</t>
    <t s="19">And with this, it will be understood why, after the aforementioned discourse brings the interpretation of the Emek HaMelech that "The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established" refers to the future Holy Temple, he adds that the implication from the Gemara and Midrashim is that it refers to the Mishkan and the Temple</t>
    <t s="20">(even though this interpretation seemingly does not relate to the content of the matter explained in this discourse),</t>
    <t s="21">because the fact that regarding "The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established" there are these two interpretations</t>
    <t s="22">(that it refers to the future Holy Temple,</t>
    <t s="23">and that it refers to the Mishkan and the Temple)</t>
    <t s="24">is</t>
    <t s="25">because in the First Temple and the Second Temple</t>
    <t s="26">(and likewise in the Mishkan)</t>
    <t s="27">there was a foretaste of the future Holy Temple, as mentioned above.</t>
    <t s="28">And therefore, the discourse also brings the interpretation that "The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established" refers to the Mishkan and the Temple,</t>
    <t s="29">for through this it explains</t>
    <t s="30">that the power that exists in this exile for the service to draw down the third Holy Temple comes from the First Temple and the Second Temple</t>
    <t s="31">(and also from the Mishkan).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the true concept of "The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established" is specifically in the future Holy Temple, where the aspect of Keter above the chain of descent will be revealed, achieved through the descent of exile.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">However, the main concept of "The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established" is specifically in the future Holy Temple.</t>
    <t s="1">In contrast, in the Mishkan and the Temple</t>
    <t s="2">(the First Temple and the Second Temple)</t>
    <t s="3">it is only a foretaste of the future Holy Temple.</t>
    <t s="4">For the interpretation of "Your hands have established" is that it is made by the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself,</t>
    <t s="5">i.e., the aspect of the Keter that is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="6">and the revelation of this aspect will be in the future Holy Temple,</t>
    <t s="7">for then specifically will there be the true concept of "the moon will stand in its perfection,"</t>
    <t s="8">the aspect of perfection that is above the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="9">For the aspect of "the moon will stand in its perfection" that was in the First Temple</t>
    <t s="10">[as our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="11">that the Holy Temple was built by Shlomo,</t>
    <t s="12">because Shlomo was in the fifteenth generation from Avraham, and then the disk of the moon was filled],</t>
    <t s="13">is analogous to the aspect of "the advantage of the land,"</t>
    <t s="14">but the perfection of the future Holy Temple is the matter of "a king is subjugated to the field."</t>
    <t s="15">And in order to draw down the aspect of "a king is subjugated to the field" as it is in its superiority,</t>
    <t s="16">it was necessary for there to be first the exile,</t>
    <t s="17">the aspect of "a king is subjugated to the field" as it is in its inferiority.</t>
    <t s="18">And through the descent of Malchus to the very lowest extreme,</t>
    <t s="19">to the point that it is subjugated to the field of the other side,</t>
    <t s="20">there will be the ascent of Malchus to the most elevated aspect,</t>
    <t s="21">until the aspect of Atik will illuminate within it.</t>
    <t s="22">For the reason that Yerushalayim, which is the aspect of Malchus, will be called "a tranquil habitation"</t>
    <t s="23">which refers to the aspect of Atik,</t>
    <t s="24">is because of this, that within Malchus the aspect of Atik will illuminate.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
